html:
Dutch painter, born in Leiden in 1606, who worked most of his life in Amsterdam during the Dutch Golden Age. He is known for his self portraits, his strong light and shadow, and The Night Watch.

He moved to Amsterdam in the early 1630s, when the city was the trading hub of Europe (Amsterdam at the centre). Rich merchants and civic groups paid for portraits, and he was soon in demand. The Night Watch, finished in 1642, shows a city militia company setting out, full of movement instead of the usual stiff rows.

He painted, drew and made etchings, and he turned often to stories from the Bible. Across about forty years he painted himself many times, from a confident young man to a lined old one, a record no artist before him had made.

His fortunes fell. He spent beyond his means and went bankrupt in 1656, and lost his wife and later his son. He died in Amsterdam in 1669. He and Vermeer are the best known painters of the Dutch Republic.
